summary: Plan reservoir releases, unit schedules and hydropower risks through practical operating scenarios. Explore the course and its applied curriculum.
lede: Hydropower operations training helps plant managers, utility engineers and water-resource planners coordinate reservoir storage, water releases and generation. Participants practise water-balance calculations and rule-curve planning, assess inflow and unit-availability scenarios, and build dispatch schedules around operating constraints. They also document risks, clarify release responsibilities and prepare an integrated operating plan that accounts for climate variability.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who make, analyse or coordinate hydropower generation and water-release decisions. It suits those who need to connect reservoir conditions, unit availability and dispatch requirements in an operating plan.
modules: Reservoir Water Balance and Rule Curves
prerequisites: Working familiarity with hydropower operations, water-resource management or electricity generation planning is recommended. No programming is required; exercises use planning calculations and may use Excel.
topics: Water & wastewater treatment and utility management
